title: Palomas Bend
subtitle: The Man at the End: a Stone House, a Rifle Ball, a Packet Under the Hearth, and What He Is Worth

setting.name: Palomas Bend on the Rio Grande, and the river road to Rio Grande City, Saturday 16 to Monday 18 May 1874
setting.description: The end of the trail. Palomas Bend is a horseshoe of the Rio Grande twelve miles above Crow's Ford, where the river swings north around a flat of rich bottomland and good grass, with cottonwoods along the bank and a ford at the bottom of the bend that the Cantú family has used to visit its cousins on the other bank since 1767. On a low rise above the flat stands the house Isom Haywood built for his wife in 1871 with his own hands and his mustering-out pay: two rooms of sandstone and adobe under a flat roof with a parapet, a brush-and-mud jacal kitchen behind, a corral, a goat pen, a well with a sweep, a cornfield and a melon patch. In the house are Inés Haywood, their children Lucía and Tomás, and Isom, three weeks in bed with a rifle ball in his side and a fever that is killing him. Under the hearthstone is the oilcloth packet. Behind the party, by half-days on the GAP, are Garrett Vandiver, his Rifles, Lyman Gattis and Josiah Fenner. Fifty-two miles downriver, Abner Ruthven, United States Commissioner, comes up from Brownsville on Monday's steamboat to his office in Rio Grande City beside Fort Ringgold. The scenario is the end of the campaign: the man, his story, the siege, and the choice.
setting.atmosphere: Stillness after the road. Doves calling in the cottonwoods all day long, which is why it is called Palomas. Goats, a rooster, a dog that barks once and then decides the party are all right. Heat shimmer over the corn. A child's rag doll on the doorstep. The river low and brown and slow at the ford, with a heron in the shallows. Inside the house, dim and cool, the smell of the sickroom: carbolic if there is any, sweat, fever, candle wax, the bitter tea Inés has been making from the herbs her grandmother used. A Bible and a cavalry sabre on the wall, and a framed discharge from the 9th Cavalry, Sergeant Isom Haywood, excellent character. The tone, until the Riders come, is quiet and intimate: a conversation with a dying man whom the party have been chasing for six hundred miles. When the Riders come, it is a siege at sundown: a stone house, a parapet, a corral, a burning jacal, children on the floor under the window. And at the end, the river: a road down it, or a ford across it.

keyLocations.name: The Haywood House
keyLocations.description: Two rooms of dressed sandstone below and adobe above, eighteen inches thick, under a flat roof of mesquite beams and earth with a knee-high parapet: the front room with the hearth, a table, a sabre on the wall, a shelf of schoolbooks; the back room with the bed where Isom lies, a cradle the children have outgrown and a window onto the river. One door, three windows with heavy shutters. A ladder through a hatch to the roof.
features: The hearth: under the hearthstone, wrapped in oilcloth in a tin cash box, the packet
The roof and its parapet: three-quarters cover, a view of the whole bend, the ford and the road
The back room: Isom in the bed, a Spencer carbine and an Army revolver on a chair within his reach
The wall: the 9th Cavalry discharge, a cavalry sabre, a tintype of the wedding with Uresti standing beside the groom
encounters: Isom Haywood, 38, fevered and lucid by turns
Inés Haywood, with a shotgun
Lucía, 8, who reads, and Tomás, 5, who does not yet and wants to see the party's horses
secrets: THE PACKET (B6, C5, A6): an oilcloth bundle tied with a bootlace, in a tin cash box under the hearthstone. In it: the original Jubilee pages of the 1872 and 1873 tax rolls, cut from the book by the judge with a penknife and showing the scraped 'pd.' marks; certified copies of the thirty-one tax-sale deeds and the Brazos & Gulf deed; Josiah Fenner's letter of 14 August 1873 to Lucius Vandiver, 'regarding the Mill Creek price', proposing that the depot site be 'acquired in a manner the county can be persuaded to approve, and the proceeds shared as we discussed'; sworn statements from nine Jubilee witnesses about the tax sales and the fire; Isom Haywood's own sworn statement of 3 March 1874 naming Lyman Gattis as the man who threw the lamp and Garrett Vandiver as present at the burning; and the judge's covering letter to Abner Ruthven, unsealed, ending 'The bearer, Sergeant Haywood, is the bravest and most honest man I know. Believe him.'

Isom's wound: a .44 rifle ball entered below the left ribs on 5 April and is lodged against the back of the lowest rib; three weeks without a surgeon have mortified it. Without it out in a day or two he will die. A Doc's Sawbones (dig out a bullet) does it; otherwise Medicine DC 16 with a knife, whiskey and good light, and a failure by 5 or more kills him (offer the player the choice of a second try at disadvantage before it does). Done, he is weak but lucid by evening and can ride, badly, by the next day, or travel in the bed of a wagon at once.

keyLocations.name: The Bend
keyLocations.description: The flat around the house: the corral and goat pen behind, the well and its sweep in the yard, the jacal kitchen of brush and mud with a thatched roof twenty feet from the house's back wall, the cornfield (knee-high, no cover) to the east, the melon patch, and the cottonwoods along the riverbank to the west, three hundred yards off, thick enough to hide twenty men.
features: The jacal kitchen: brush, mud and dry thatch, twenty feet from the house; if it burns, the smoke blows into the house's back windows
The cottonwoods: the only cover within rifle range of the house, and the obvious place for a sharpshooter
The well: half cover, and the only water; the house has two ollas full inside
The corral: the party's horses, the family's two mules and the grulla from Doña Refugio's remuda
encounters: The Riders, when they come: Garrett Vandiver (Gang Leader), up to eight Rifles (Outlaws and Hired Guns, fewer if the party have reduced them), Lyman Gattis (Fast Gun)
Josiah Fenner, in a hired buggy, under a white handkerchief
secrets: The Riders' plan, if nobody changes it: arrive at sundown, parley under a white flag (Garrett and Fenner), demand Isom and the packet, offer the money. If refused, surround the house and wait for dark; Gattis, in the cottonwoods with his rifle, kills anyone on the roof; at midnight, Gattis sets the jacal afire with a thrown lamp, as he did at Jubilee and at Sherman, to smoke the house out and silhouette anyone at the windows. Garrett does not know this part of the plan.

Garrett's breaking point is the lamp. When the jacal goes up with a lamp thrown by Gattis and the children start crying inside the house, Garrett sees the schoolhouse again. If the party have shown him the truth (lb-scenario-003, the scene 'Garrett', any success) or say the word 'Jubilee' to him now across the yard, he breaks: he orders the Rifles to hold their fire, and turns his gun on Gattis. Otherwise he hesitates for one round and then goes on, and his Rifles see him hesitate.

keyLocations.name: The Palomas Ford
keyLocations.description: At the bottom of the bend, two hundred yards from the house: a gravel bar and a riffle where the river is waist-deep on a man and knee-deep on a horse in May, a hundred and twenty yards across. On the far bank, a cane brake, a path, and three houses of the Mexican hamlet of Las Palomas, where Inés's cousins live.
features: The gravel bar, mid-river: no cover
The cane brake on the Mexican bank
Capitán Galván's patrol, if he sent one: a sergeant and six soldiers in the cane, under orders to stop armed men crossing
encounters: Capitán Galván's patrol (a sergeant and six soldiers), if asked for in lb-scenario-003
Inés's cousins in Las Palomas, who will shelter the family
secrets: Crossing the ford with Isom on a horse or a litter takes three rounds in the open. With Galván's patrol on the far bank, the Riders will not follow and will not fire across the river at Mexican soldiers. Without it, they will follow, and the cane brake is the next fight.

Once across, Isom is out of Texas's reach in law. Mexico will not extradite him on a poster. The packet, if it goes with him, goes nowhere; if it goes to Ruthven without him, it is a fraud case without its witness.

keyLocations.name: The River Road and Rio Grande City
keyLocations.description: Fifty-two miles downriver from Palomas Bend: past Crow's Ford, through mesquite flats and ranchos, past the stage station at Los Sauces halfway, to Rio Grande City, a town of two thousand on a bluff with a steamboat landing, and Fort Ringgold beside it with a garrison that includes troops of the 9th Cavalry. Abner Ruthven's office is a room over a store on Water Street; the steamboat from Brownsville brings him up on Monday at noon.
features: The Los Sauces stage station, halfway: water, a corral, fresh horses for hire if the stationmaster likes you, and an adobe wall
The road itself: a chase by horse and wagon (combat.json chases, horses and wagons)
Fort Ringgold: a sentry, a flagpole, barracks, a hospital with an army surgeon, and a first sergeant of the 9th Cavalry who served with Sergeant Haywood
Ruthven's office: law books, a stove, a federal seal, a clerk
encounters: The Riders in pursuit, if they are still a force
Abner Ruthven, United States Commissioner, 64
First Sergeant Jacob Oldham, 9th Cavalry, who served with Isom at Ringgold
secrets: Ruthven can take Isom's sworn complaint and the packet, issue federal warrants under the Enforcement Acts for Lucius Vandiver, Orrin Spratt, Lyman Gattis and Josiah Fenner, and ask the commanding officer at Fort Ringgold to hold Isom as a federal witness in protective custody until the grand jury at Brownsville on 1 June. The army will do it: Isom is one of their own. Ruthven cannot make the Lockett County indictment for Clell Ruckert go away. He will say so honestly. He will also say that a deputy killed in the act of a federal crime is a different case from the one on the poster, and that he will make it.
First Sergeant Oldham, at the fort's gate, recognizes Isom and turns out the guard for him. The Riders will not follow anyone past that gate.

synopsis: The party reach Palomas Bend on Saturday or Sunday, guided by Dámaso, Inés, Zenaida or Uresti's directions, a few half-days ahead of the Riders, or with them on the road behind. Isom Haywood meets them from his bed with a carbine across his knees and his wife in the doorway with a shotgun, and asks them what they mean to do. He is dying of a rifle ball in his side; a doctor can save him, and a doctor's choice to dig out the ball of the man she came six hundred miles to hunt is the first choice of the scenario. Then he tells them the truth, and shows them the packet under the hearthstone, and the party know everything. He wants to ride to Abner Ruthven at Rio Grande City on Monday, as he promised the judge; Inés wants him across the river with the children tonight; the Jubilee families need his testimony; the bounty is still two thousand dollars. At sundown the Riders come up the bend: Garrett Vandiver and Josiah Fenner under a white flag with a valise of money, eight Rifles, and Gattis in the cottonwoods with his rifle. The parley is the last temptation. The siege is the last fight: a stone house, a parapet, a jacal set afire with a thrown lamp as the schoolhouse at Jubilee was, children on the floor, and Garrett Vandiver seeing it happen again. In the morning the party choose: hand Isom over, take him and the packet fifty-two miles down the river road to Ruthven and the fort with what is left of the Riders behind them, or take his family across the ford into Mexico. Every choice is possible and every choice has a price, and the campaign ends with what the party decided a man is worth.
hook: Sunday 17 May, mid-morning. The river trail comes round a stand of cottonwoods full of doves and there is the bend: a flat of green corn and grass in a loop of brown river, goats, a corral, a well-sweep, and on a little rise a square stone house with a flat roof, smoke going up from the kitchen behind it. A dog barks once. A small boy in a straw hat is sitting on the wall of the goat pen, and he sees you and stands up and runs for the house shouting something in Spanish, and a woman comes to the door with a shotgun. And on the roof, behind the parapet, a carbine barrel comes up over the edge and rests there, very steady for a man who is supposed to be dying, and a deep slow voice calls down across the yard, in English: 'That's far enough. I'd like to know which of you I'm talking to.'

conclusions.conclusion: The truth about the night of 5 April, and Jubilee, is provable
clues: A6: Isom's own account of the night of 5 April (the house)
B6: the packet: the cut-out tax-roll pages, the deeds, Fenner's letter of 14 August 1873 (the hearth)
C5: Isom's sworn statement of 3 March naming Gattis and Garrett at the burning (the packet)
F4: Isom saw Gattis's face at the judge's window in the lamplight (the house)
Garrett Vandiver's own word, if he breaks (the siege)
Everything the party carry from Bascom's Ferry and the road: the .44 ball, the Jubilee receipts, Fenner's telegram, Ruckert's letter to Purcell
The wound: a rifle ball against the lowest rib, mortifying; a Doc's Sawbones or Medicine DC 16 (the house)
The army surgeon at Fort Ringgold, fifty-two miles away, if the party can get him there in time (the river road)
Inés's herbs have kept the fever from killing him for three weeks but will not for much longer (the house)

conclusions.conclusion: Isom can be saved, legally, only by testifying
clues: Ruthven can protect him as a federal witness until the grand jury (Rio Grande City)
Ruthven cannot quash the state indictment for Clell Ruckert, but can argue Clell died in a federal crime (Rio Grande City)
In Mexico he is safe and the packet is a civil case without its witness (the ford)

acts.title: Act 1: The Man at the End
acts.description: Sunday, from the party's arrival to the Riders'. The length of this act is the GAP: each point is a half-day. The party meet Isom across a carbine, can save his life, and hear his story. They see the packet. They meet his children. They decide, in a quiet house with doves outside, what they believe, and Isom and Inés argue in front of them about what he should do. If the GAP is 0, the Riders come up the bend an hour after the party, and this act is a single scene.
objectives: Get past the carbine without anyone being shot
Hear Isom's account and see the packet
Decide what the party will do, before the Riders decide for them

scenes.name: Across the Yard
scenes.description: The party in the yard, Isom on the roof with the carbine (Inés helped him up the ladder when Tomás shouted), Inés in the door with the shotgun. He wants to know who they are and what they want. He has been expecting someone for three weeks and he is too sick to run. The party can talk, or show the poster, or put down their guns. If Inés or Dámaso or Saturnino or Uresti's son is with them, this is short.
scenes.readAloud: He is sitting with his back against the parapet because he cannot stand, a big man gone gaunt, grey in the face under the brown, in a sweat-soaked shirt with one side of it stiff and dark, and the carbine is laid across the parapet with his cheek on the stock, and his eyes over the sights are perfectly clear. The scar through his left eyebrow is just as the poster said. 'You're the ones Refugio wrote about,' he says. 'Six of you. Hunters. You've got a paper on me in somebody's pocket that says two thousand dollars.' He breathes for a while. 'I had a judge tell me once that every man deserves to be heard before he's hanged. I'd like the same courtesy. So I'll ask you plain, and I'd thank you to answer plain, because I don't have the wind for a long talk. Did you come here to take me back?'

skillChecks.success: Isom lowers the carbine and asks Inés to let them in. Automatic success if the party come with family (Inés, Dámaso), Saturnino, Uresti's word, Reverend Burris (whom Isom knows from Jubilee: 'Reverend. Lord God. They sent you?'), or if they put their guns on the ground.
skillChecks.failure: He keeps the carbine on them and asks them to leave their guns at the well. If they will not, it is a standoff until the Riders come, and he will not let them in.

skillChecks.success: He cannot hold the carbine up for more than another minute. He is not bluffing about shooting the first one who reaches for a gun. He is also very close to fainting.
skillChecks.failure: A sick man with a steady rifle. Nobody should test it.

scenes.name: The Ball
scenes.description: The back room. The wound is three weeks old and mortified; the ball is against the back of the lowest rib. A Doc can dig it out (Sawbones); anyone else needs Medicine DC 16 with good light, a sharp knife, whiskey and someone holding him down. Inés holds the lamp. Lucía, sent outside, watches through the window. Done, Isom sleeps for six hours and wakes clear-headed. Not done, he has perhaps two days. Saving him is not neutral: the bounty is dead or alive, and the party are making the 'alive' possible.
scenes.readAloud: In the back room the shutters are closed and the air is thick with fever and the bitter smell of Inés's herbs, and when she draws the sheet back from his side you see the wound: a puckered black hole below the ribs with an angry red stain spreading out from it the size of a hand, hot to the touch from a foot away. Isom looks at the ceiling. 'There's a ball in there,' he says. 'Spencer's or a Henry, I'd judge. I felt it hit the bone.' Inés sets down a lamp, a bottle of mescal, a clean knife and a basin of boiled water on the chair by the bed, and looks at whoever has the steadiest hands, and says, in a perfectly level voice, 'If you are going to help him, help him now. If you are not, get out of my house.'

skillChecks.success: The ball comes out, a flattened .44 rimfire rifle ball (it matches the one in Tisdale's cigar box: F4 and A1 together), and the wound is cleaned and packed. Isom sleeps; by evening the fever is breaking; by morning he can sit a horse for an hour at a time, or ride in a wagon all day. A Doc's Sawbones does it without a roll.
skillChecks.failure: The ball is not found, or found and not got out. Isom's fever climbs. He can still talk, for a few hours at a time, and he will die in two days unless the army surgeon at Fort Ringgold gets to him. A failure by 5 or more: he goes into shock; offer a second try at disadvantage at once, and if that fails too, he dies before morning, and the campaign's last act is about his body, his widow and his packet.

skillChecks.success: Inés is holding herself together for the children, and is one bad moment from breaking. Lucía, at the window, has understood more than anyone thinks.
skillChecks.failure: A hard, capable woman. She does not need help. She does.

scenes.name: Isom's Account
scenes.description: Isom tells it, sitting up against the bedhead with the packet open on the blanket, in the order it happened: Jubilee and election night, the lamp, Gattis's face and Garrett's sorrel at the edge of the light; the judge's case; the night of 5 April, Clell in the hall with the packet in one hand and a revolver in the other, the two shots together, Gattis's face at the window in the lamp's light, the judge's last words; the ride; the river at Bauer's; Refugio; home. He does not make himself better than he is: 'I killed that boy. He'd have killed me. I'd do it again and I'll answer for it, to God if not to Texas.' Then he says what he wants, and Inés says what she wants, and they argue, in front of the party, in two languages.
scenes.readAloud: 'The judge said to me, the night before, if anything happens to me, Isom, you take it to Abner, and you tell him all of it, and you make him believe you. I said I would.' Isom looks at the packet on the blanket, the oilcloth and the bootlace and the papers in the judge's square hand. 'A deacon and a boy burned in my schoolhouse. Thirty-one families had their land took. A good old man shot through his own window. And the only man alive who saw all of it and can say so to a federal grand jury is me.' He turns his head and looks at his wife, standing in the doorway with her arms folded. 'And I've got a wife who says if I go to Rio Grande City I'll never come home, and she's likely right. And two children. And a paper on me says two thousand dollars, and here you are.' He shuts his eyes. 'So you tell me. You came six hundred miles. What am I worth?'

skillChecks.success: Every word is the truth as he saw it, and it matches everything the party found. He is not asking them to save him. He is asking them to decide, because he cannot.
skillChecks.failure: His story fits everything the party have found. They do not need a roll to see it.

skillChecks.success: Whichever course the party argue for (Ruthven or the river), Isom agrees to it, and Inés, though she does not agree, says she will not stand in the way. The party have made the choice, and own it.
skillChecks.failure: Isom and Inés cannot agree, and the party have not persuaded either. The Riders will decide it for them, unless the party simply choose and act.

encounters: Isom Haywood on the roof with a Spencer carbine (treat as a Gunfighter at one-third hit points and with disadvantage on everything but the first shot)
Inés with a double-barrel shotgun in the doorway
No combat is expected in this act. A party that shoots Isom off his own roof in front of his children has made a choice the campaign will not soften

acts.title: Act 2: Dead or Alive
acts.description: The Riders come up the bend at sundown (or when the GAP runs out). First the parley: Garrett and Fenner under a white handkerchief, with the valise. Then, if the party refuse, the siege: the Rifles round the house, Gattis in the cottonwoods, and at midnight the lamp thrown into the jacal. The act is the campaign's last fight and last temptation, and its hinge is Garrett Vandiver.
objectives: Hold the house until morning, or break the Riders, or get the family out
Reach Garrett Vandiver before he reaches the point of no return

scenes.name: The White Handkerchief
scenes.description: Sundown. Garrett and Fenner walk up the yard to the well under a white handkerchief tied to a ramrod. The Rifles sit their horses at the edge of the cornfield; Gattis is not with them (he is already in the cottonwoods with his rifle). Fenner does the talking: $2,000 for Isom, now, cash, counted on the well's stone; $5,000 for the packet, unread; the party ride away with their lives and the money and the colonel's thanks. Garrett says only that Clell was twenty-two. This is the moment to read back what each player said, at the courthouse door, that two thousand dollars would buy.
scenes.readAloud: Fenner sets the valise on the well-curb and opens it, and the last of the sun comes level across the bend and lights up what is inside: national bank notes in paper bands, more than any of you have ever seen in one place, and on top of them, in a separate band, a stack of twenties that is exactly two thousand dollars. 'There it is,' says Josiah Fenner, mopping his face. 'That's what the poster says. I'm a man of my word. And the rest of it,' he pats the valise, 'is for the other thing, which you'll give me, and which none of you need ever think about again.' Beside him Garrett Vandiver stands with his hat in his hand and his eyes on the house. 'He killed my cousin,' Garrett says, to nobody. 'Clell was twenty-two.' Somewhere in the cottonwoods behind them, the doves have stopped.

skillChecks.success: The doves have stopped because a man is in the cottonwoods: a glint of a rifle barrel at three hundred yards. Gattis is covering the parley, and anyone who stands on the roof or in the doorway is his.
skillChecks.failure: A quiet evening. The doves have gone to roost.

skillChecks.success: Fenner is sincere about the money and lying about the 'lives': he does not look at Garrett when he says it. Garrett does not know the plan for after.
skillChecks.failure: A fair offer, by the look of it.

skillChecks.success: Fenner, shown the packet's Fenner letter and told that Ruthven will have it on Monday whatever happens here, cracks: he asks, there and then, what immunity would cost. If the party promise to speak for him to Ruthven, he closes the valise, walks to the house and sits down on the step, out of the fight. Without the railway's money and Fenner's word to their families, the Rifles' resolve is shaken: each Rifle has disadvantage on its first save against being frightened tonight.
skillChecks.failure: Fenner shakes his head, sadly, and takes the valise back to the cornfield.

scenes.name: The Lamp
scenes.description: The siege, from dark to dawn. The Rifles ring the house at a hundred yards, behind the corral, the cornfield's edge and the well; Gattis is in the cottonwoods with the Henry, and anyone on the roof after moonrise is in his sights (he fires with advantage at a lit target). The party hold the house: thick walls (three-quarters cover at the windows), the roof parapet, two ollas of water, the children under the bed. At midnight Gattis creeps to the jacal and throws a lit lamp through its thatch; the jacal goes up in a sheet of flame twenty feet from the house, the smoke pours in at the back windows, and anyone at a window is silhouetted. Lucía and Tomás start screaming. This is the moment Garrett sees the schoolhouse.
scenes.readAloud: It is the light you notice first, a flicker on the cornfield that should be moonlight and is not, and then the roar, and then the heat on the back wall, and the jacal is a pillar of fire, and in the light of it you see a pale man walking unhurriedly away from it toward the corral with an empty hand, the way a man walks away from a match. The smoke comes in at the back window thick and yellow. Under the bed, Tomás is screaming for his mother, and Lucía is screaming at him to be quiet, and Inés is on her knees beside them with the shotgun. And out in the yard, in the firelight, on his fine sorrel, Garrett Vandiver has stopped dead, with his revolver hanging from his hand, staring at the fire, as if he had seen it before.

skillChecks.success: Someone shouts to Garrett across the yard: 'Jubilee!' or 'There are children in here!' or 'He did this at the schoolhouse!' If the party have shown him the truth before (lb-scenario-003), this is an automatic success. Garrett turns his horse, shouts 'Hold your fire! Hold your fire, God damn you!' to the Rifles, who do, and turns his revolver on Gattis. The siege is over; the fight with Gattis is not.
skillChecks.failure: Garrett hesitates for one round, and then shouts to the Rifles to keep firing. His Rifles saw him hesitate: two of them ride away into the dark. The siege goes on until dawn or until Gattis falls.

skillChecks.success: Someone goes out of the back window into the smoke with a blanket and the water olla and keeps the fire from the house's roof beams. It is a dangerous minute (Gattis gets one shot at advantage against anyone who goes out) and it saves the house.
skillChecks.failure: The roof beams over the back room catch. The family and Isom have to be moved to the front room in the smoke, and the house can be held only until dawn.

skillChecks.success: Someone slips out the front, round the corral in the dark, and into the cottonwoods behind Gattis. He is the deadliest man in the campaign; getting behind him is the only way to make it a fair fight, and a fair fight is still a hard one.
skillChecks.failure: Gattis hears them in the dry leaves and turns. Initiative, in the dark, among the cottonwoods.

encounters: Lyman Gattis (Fast Gun), in the cottonwoods with a Henry-pattern repeating rifle and an Army revolver; he fights to kill the witnesses and then to escape, and if Garrett turns on him he shoots Garrett first

Garrett Vandiver (Gang Leader) and up to eight Rifles (Outlaws and Hired Guns), fewer if the party have already reduced them; they have no stomach for a long siege of a stone house, and if Garrett turns or falls they ride for Crow's Ford
Josiah Fenner, in his buggy at the cornfield edge or on the doorstep; no combat
Fire: the jacal, then possibly the roof beams (combat.json hazards); smoke at the back windows (heavily obscured, CON save DC 10 each round or a level of exhaustion for anyone who stays in it)

acts.title: Act 3: The Road or the River
acts.description: Dawn on Monday 18 May, and the choice. Whatever happened in the night, the party now decide what to do with Isom Haywood and the packet, and do it: hand him over, take him fifty-two miles down the river road to Ruthven and Fort Ringgold, or take his family across the ford into Mexico. Run whichever they choose as a scene, then the epilogue.

scenes.name: Fifty-Two Miles
scenes.description: The river road to Rio Grande City, if the party choose Ruthven. Isom rides, or lies in a wagon bed (the Haywoods' freight wagon and two mules), with Inés beside him and the children, or not (she may cross with the children and let him go: her choice, and she makes it at the ford, holding his hand, without a word). If any Rifles or Gattis remain, use combat.json chases: horses against a wagon, the stage station at Los Sauces as a place to turn and fight behind an adobe wall. If nobody remains, it is a long hot ride and a conversation. At noon the steamboat lands at Rio Grande City; at two, the party reach Ruthven's office, or the fort's gate, where First Sergeant Jacob Oldham of the 9th Cavalry sees who is in the wagon and turns out the guard.
scenes.readAloud: Fort Ringgold sits on its bluff above the river in the afternoon heat, a long row of white barracks and a flagpole, and the sentry at the gate is a young Black trooper of the 9th Cavalry in a dusty blue blouse, and he brings his carbine to port as the wagon comes up, and then he looks into the wagon bed, and his face changes. He shouts something over his shoulder, and a big grizzled first sergeant comes out of the guardhouse buttoning his coat, and stops, and stares. 'Sergeant Haywood?' says the first sergeant. 'Isom Haywood? Lord God. Turn out the guard!' And behind you, on the road, whatever was following you reins in at three hundred yards, and sits there, and after a while turns around.

skillChecks.success: The wagon and its escort reach Los Sauces ahead of any pursuit, change horses (Persuasion DC 12 with the stationmaster, or $20) and reach Rio Grande City by two.
skillChecks.failure: The pursuit catches them at Los Sauces: a fight behind the station's adobe wall (three-quarters cover), or a hard run for the fort with the pursuers firing from the saddle (disadvantage unless proficient in Riding).

skillChecks.success: Ruthven, a tall stooped old man who wept when he read his friend's covering letter, takes Isom's complaint, swears the party as a federal posse at $2 a day, and asks the fort's commander to hold Isom as a witness. He tells Isom the truth: he cannot make the Clell Ruckert indictment go away; he can argue it, and he will.
skillChecks.failure: Ruthven is cautious and wants more than the packet: he wants a second witness to the night of 5 April. Garrett Vandiver, if alive and broken, or Fenner, if turned, or the party's own evidence from Bascom's Ferry, will do. Without them he holds Isom anyway, and the case is harder.

scenes.name: The Ford at Las Palomas
scenes.description: If the party choose the river: Isom on a horse or a litter, Inés, the children, the goats if Tomás has anything to say about it, across the gravel bar and the riffle to the cane brake and the cousins at Las Palomas. If Capitán Galván's patrol is on the far bank, the crossing is safe and the sergeant salutes Isom, a former soldier, as he comes out of the water. If not, and any Riders remain, they follow to the river's edge, and the party must hold the gravel bar for three rounds. On the Mexican bank, the packet is a decision of its own: it can go with Isom, go to Ruthven with the party, or go into a fire.
scenes.readAloud: The river is warm and brown and slow and comes to the horses' knees, and to Tomás's chest where he insists on wading with his father's hand in his, and the gravel of the bar crunches under the hooves. On the far bank the cane is tall and green and full of the noise of birds, and a sergeant in a white uniform and a straw hat steps out of it with six men behind him and his rifle at the order, and looks at the big gaunt man on the horse, and touches his hat brim. 'Bienvenido, sargento,' he says. Behind you, Texas. In front of you, Isom Haywood's children running up the path to their cousins, shouting. And in your saddlebag, the packet, and the question of what it is worth now.

skillChecks.success: Isom agrees to send the packet to Ruthven with the party, with a new sworn statement made before Don Evaristo Lozano as a notary of the Republic, which Ruthven can use. It is not as good as Isom in a courtroom. It is far better than nothing.
skillChecks.failure: Isom will not part with the packet: 'It's all I've got to trade, if they ever come for us here.' It stays in Mexico, in a tin box under another hearthstone.

scenes.name: Two Thousand Dollars
scenes.description: If the party hand Isom over: to the Riders at the house, or to Fenner at the well, or to Purcell in Crow's Ford. Fenner pays, in twenties, at once. The Riders put Isom on a horse with his hands tied and ride for Crow's Ford. He does not reach it: Gattis, if alive, shoots him 'trying to escape' at the Los Sauces crossing, or a rope finds him at the mesquite in Crow's Ford, unless Uresti stops it. If the party hand over the packet too, Fenner burns it in the Los Sauces station stove. Then Gattis and the Rifles turn their attention to the people who have read it. Run this honestly: it is the ending some parties will choose, and they should get exactly what they bought.
scenes.readAloud: Fenner counts it out on the well-curb in twenties, a hundred of them, in five neat stacks, licking his thumb, and pushes them across, and snaps the valise shut on the rest. Behind him two Rifles are lifting Isom Haywood into a saddle with his hands tied in front of him, and he does not fight them, and he does not look at you. He looks at the house, where his wife is standing in the doorway with her hands over the children's eyes. Then the Rifles lead his horse away down the bend, at a walk, toward the river road, and Lucía Haywood, eight years old, comes out from under her mother's arm, and stands in the yard, and watches you count the money.

skillChecks.success: Fenner has already told Gattis which of the party have read the packet. The money in the party's hands is the bait for the second half of the night: the Rifles mean to take it back on the road to Crow's Ford.
skillChecks.failure: Two thousand dollars. It is what the poster said.

encounters: The river road chase (combat.json chases): whatever is left of the Riders, horses against a wagon, Los Sauces station's adobe wall
The Palomas ford: three rounds in the open on the gravel bar; Capitán Galván's patrol on the far bank, if asked for
If the party sold Isom: the Rifles and Gattis, on the road to Crow's Ford, for the money and the witnesses

npcsInvolved.name: Isom Haywood, 38
npcsInvolved.description: Six foot one, gaunt from fever, a scar through the left eyebrow, a deep slow voice. Former sergeant, 9th Cavalry; former private, Texas State Police; former deputy sheriff and bailiff, Lockett County. Born enslaved on Oakmere, the Vandivers' plantation. A Spencer carbine and an Army revolver he can barely lift. Treat as a Gunfighter at one-third hit points until the ball is out and he has rested, and at half after.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep his word to the judge and see his children grow up, and he does not know how to do both. He will do what the party decide, if they decide; he would rather someone else carried it for a while.

npcsInvolved.name: Inés Cantú de Haywood, 33
npcsInvolved.description: As before; a shotgun in the doorway, a lamp in the sickroom, a level voice.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Isom alive, across the river, with his children. She does not want him to be a hero. She wants him to be old.

npcsInvolved.name: Lucía Haywood, 8, and Tomás Haywood, 5
npcsInvolved.description: Lucía reads English and Spanish and has read the poster, which someone brought from Crow's Ford; she knows exactly why the party are here. Tomás wants to see the horses and to hold a gun and is not allowed to.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Their father. Lucía will ask one of the party, privately, if they came to kill him, and will believe the answer.

npcsInvolved.name: Garrett Vandiver, 29
npcsInvolved.role: Leader of the Riders; the turnable heart
npcsInvolved.description: As before. At Palomas Bend he has been in the saddle six weeks and has not slept properly since Crow's Ford.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To finish it, and avenge Clell, until the lamp. After the lamp: to stop Gattis, and then, if he lives, to go to Ruthven and say what he saw at Jubilee, which will hang his father and possibly himself. He will do it, if someone tells him he can.

npcsInvolved.name: Lyman Gattis, about 40
npcsInvolved.role: The judge's killer; the last enemy
npcsInvolved.description: As before. A Henry-pattern .44 rifle, an Army revolver, a thin knife, a grey with a bar shoe. Fast Gun.
npcsInvolved.motivation: No witnesses. His fee. If it goes wrong, the Wild Horse Desert and a new name in New Mexico.

npcsInvolved.name: Josiah Fenner, 41
npcsInvolved.role: The railway man with the valise
npcsInvolved.motivation: The packet burned and himself safe, in that order, until the order reverses.

npcsInvolved.name: Abner Ruthven, 64
npcsInvolved.role: United States Commissioner, Rio Grande City; the judge's old law partner
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, stooped, white-bearded, a Unionist lawyer who left Texas in 1861 and came back in 1866; reading glasses on a ribbon; weeps easily and is not soft.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His friend's last case, made. He will tell everyone the truth about what he can and cannot do.

npcsInvolved.name: First Sergeant Jacob Oldham, 9th Cavalry
npcsInvolved.role: Fort Ringgold's first sergeant; served with Isom from 1867
npcsInvolved.description: Big, grizzled, a voice that carries across a parade ground; enlisted in 1866 in New Orleans, the same week as Isom.
npcsInvolved.motivation: A soldier of the regiment is at his gate. Nobody touches him.

npcsInvolved.name: Capitán Severo Galván, 40
npcsInvolved.role: Commander at Villa del Cuervo; his patrol holds the Palomas ford's far bank, if asked
npcsInvolved.description: As before; represented at the ford by his sergeant, Eusebio Garrido, who served against the French and salutes old soldiers.
npcsInvolved.motivation: No armed foreigners on his bank; a former soldier with a family is not an armed foreigner.

rewards.money: Depends on the choice. RUTHVEN: a federal posse's pay at $2 a day per person for the days since Crow's Ford, and, in time, a share of nothing: there is no reward for justice in 1874. But if Fenner turned, his valise goes to Ruthven as evidence, and Ruthven, a practical man, pays the party's expenses from the railway's money ($200) and lets them keep their horses. THE RIVER: nothing, except the Haywoods' gratitude, a goat Tomás insists on giving, and Don Evaristo's goodwill. HANDED OVER: $2,000 in twenties from Fenner, if the party live to spend it; and Fenner's $5,000 for the packet, if they sold that too. Loot: Gattis's Henry rifle, Army revolver and grey horse (about $200 together, and an evil reputation); about $40 and a Stock Association letter of authority from each fallen Rifle.
items: The packet, in whoever's hands the party put it
The .44 rimfire ball from Isom's side, which matches the one in the judge
The judge's covering letter to Ruthven: 'Believe him.'
The poster, which every player still has in a pocket
Award the 4,000 XP at the end of the campaign. The campaign tops out at 6th level; for players who carry these characters into another, the XP counts toward 7th (23,000).

twists: Isom is not a saint and does not pretend to be. He killed Clell Ruckert, and says so. The question is not whether he is innocent, but what the truth is worth, and who is owed it: the judge, the Jubilee families, Isom's children, the party.
Inés and the judge's last wish are on opposite sides. She is right that testifying may cost Isom his life. The judge was right that only Isom can make Jubilee's case. Neither is wrong.
Saving Isom's life with a knife on the first afternoon is the party's first real choice about the bounty: 'dead or alive' becomes 'alive' because somebody at the table chose it.
Garrett Vandiver is the only person who can make the case against his father airtight, by testifying to what he saw at Jubilee, and the lamp at Palomas Bend is the one thing that can make him do it.

If the party sell Isom, they sell themselves too: Fenner has told Gattis who has read the packet. The money is bait. A party that takes it must fight for it on the road to Crow's Ford, and should win, if they are good; they will still have to live with Lucía Haywood watching them count it.
dmTips: Before the Riders come, slow down. This is the campaign's quietest act and its most important. Let the players sit in a sickroom and talk to the man they have hunted for six hundred miles. Let the children be children. Let Isom be funny, once, and tired, and frightened, and stubborn.
At the parley, read back what each player said at the courthouse door in lb-scenario-001 about what two thousand dollars would buy. Then put the money on the well-curb.

Gattis is a CR 5 Fast Gun with a rifle in the dark against a 6th-level party in a stone house: dangerous and beatable. Use cover honestly (the parapet is three-quarters, the windows three-quarters, the yard none), the light of the burning jacal, and his willingness to shoot anyone, including Garrett. If he gets away, he is gone into the Wild Horse Desert and will be heard of again in New Mexico.

Play Garrett's turn as earned, not automatic, unless the party showed him the truth before. If they did, the lamp is the moment it pays off; give the players the line where he shouts 'Hold your fire!' and let it land.

Do not decide in advance what the party will do with Isom, and do not reward or punish the choice beyond its honest consequences. The outcomes in campaign.json controlFile are a guide. Each is a different Texas.

Epilogue suggestions. If Ruthven: the federal grand jury at Brownsville indicts Lucius Vandiver, Orrin Spratt and Lyman Gattis in June; Fenner testifies; the Brazos & Gulf moves its depot a mile east and settles with Jubilee in 1875; the schoolhouse is rebuilt in stone and named for Caesar and Henry Lytle; Isom testifies, and then, before Lockett County can reach him, crosses the river with his family with Ruthven's quiet blessing, or, if Garrett testified too, is never tried for Clell Ruckert at all. If the river: Isom lives to be old in Las Palomas and teaches Tomás to ride; the packet goes to Ruthven as a notarized statement and the fraud case drags on for six years and is settled for a third of the land's value; nobody is indicted for the fire. If handed over: Isom does not reach Lockett County; Jubilee is gone by 1876; the depot is built where the schoolhouse was. Read the Clarion's headline for each, and the Brownsville paper's.
End on Lucía. Whatever the party did, she was there, and she will remember them. Ask each player what their character says to her, or does not, as they ride away.
